samples.summary: MCP setup CLI: remove shell-plus-UI-text payload inference
evidence: Decoded JavaScript rotates an Obfuscator string table; README discloses javascript-obfuscator and encrypted licensed bundles.
setup-wizard only invokes git remote -v, with output captured for configuration. Its long encoded strings contain interface/documentation text, not an executable stage.
Git worktree operations, AI-harness processes, updater package fetches, JWT verification, encrypted bundles and license heartbeat match the documented product.
License heartbeat sends the license token to its disclosed licensing service. No credential theft, spying, destructive behavior or covert backdoor found.
These are first-party findings; no fetched dependency caused the hostile/suspicious reports.

samples.identity: edgar-fabric-ingest: SEC-ingest TypeScript source with trojanized Windows LuaJIT sidecar
samples.summary: EDGAR Lua trojan: require deceptive ZIP promotion and real launch
evidence: Launcher.cmd starts luajit.exe libgcc.txt; the text-named file is an encrypted, VM-obfuscated Lua program. Stock LuaJIT binaries supply execution.
Reversed the string-table permutation, custom Base64 stage and seeded string cipher; recovered hundreds of seeded constants in an isolated Lua 5.1 VM with native APIs mocked.
Recovered command construction disables Defender with Add-MpPreference exclusions for the system drive and executable/DLL extensions.
Recovered persistent task commands target C:/Windows/System32/oobe/Setup.exe with /rl highest; other constants name Run keys and Windows Setup ErrorHandler.cmd.
Native stage hides its console, uses an RWX stub to retrieve the PEB, and walks module/export structures to resolve Win32 APIs.
The advertised SEC/TypeScript CLI does not disclose these Windows actions. Its README image links a raw ZIP and tells users to launch it. No family attribution asserted.

samples.identity: ASPack-packed VB6 executable infector/autorun worm posing as Microsoft Firewall
samples.summary: VB6 Firewall worm: separate PE parsing, packing and API resolution
evidence: ASPack stub unpacked in Unicorn with external APIs mocked; no native malware execution. Rizin inspected original, carved images and unpacked VB6 image.
Unpacked VB5! metadata names pjtDiskBinder, frmMain and fleInfect; executable targeting uses *.exe.
Unpacked strings and VB6 file/registry routines implement drive targeting, NTDETECT.EXE copies, autorun.inf with Shell=NTDETECT.EXE, and the HKLM Run\WinFirewall value.
False Microsoft Firewall/Xiang identity fronts a dominant overlay with multiple PE host images.
Embedded CSRSS and javapackager fragments contain mismatched/truncated host data. PEB/header checks and multiply-by-31 arithmetic alone do not demonstrate custom GetProcAddress or import hashing.
User-provided VirusTotal/sandbox reputation corroborates the malicious judgement; conviction rests on unpacked code, not the filename or ML prior.
